newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea chipmakers to be cleared of dumping charges.
newsitem.headline: SKorea chipmakers to be cleared of dumping charges.

text.p: The United States Department of Commerce is expected to clear two South Korean memory chip makers of dumping charges, the Korea International Trade Association said in a statement on Thursday.

"The Department has preliminarily determined that no dumping margins exist for both respondents. We intend not to revoke the order on DRAMs from Korea," a copy of a Department of Commerce document obtained by the association said.

The association said the department had decided to give a preliminary "de minimis" ruling on the two firms -- a 0.01 percent dumping margin on Hyundai Electronics Industries Co and 0.02 percent on LG Semicon Co.
"If these preliminary results are adopted in our final results of administrative review, we will instruct the U.S. Customs Service not to assess anti-dumping duties," it said.

The preliminary ruling, based on the department's third review of dumping charges against dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips of one megabits and above made by the two firms, is due to be released on Friday, the association said.
The association, formerly called the Korea Foreign Trade Association, said the review covered the period of May 1, 1995 through April 30, 1996.
In the second review, the department also gave a final de minimis ruling in January -- a 0.01 percent margin on Hyundai and a 0.10 percent margin on LG, the association said.
Hyundai Electronics is a unit of the Hyundai Group and LG Semicon of the LG Group.
